overview.description: Pai Gow is an ancient Chinese gambling game played with a specialized set of thirty-two Chinese domino tiles. Each player is dealt four tiles which they must partition into two separate pairs: a high-ranking hand and a low-ranking hand. The objective is to outrank both of the banker's corresponding pairs, requiring deep knowledge of the complex and non-numeric tile ranking hierarchy.

history.origins: Pai Gow (牌九) dates back to the Song Dynasty and is the ancestor of many modern partition games including Pai Gow Poker.
timeline: 19th Century: Widespread in Cantonese gambling houses.
1980s: Adapted into Pai Gow Poker in California.
Present: A core high-stakes game in Asian and global casino markets.
history.evolution: The game transitioned from traditional bone tiles to acrylic casino tiles, with standardized 'House Way' rules added for modern dealer play.
history.cultural: Regarded as a game of high prestige; skilled players can identify tiles by feeling the indentations on the tile faces.

setup.players: Up to eight players sit around a table; the role of banker rotates among players counter-clockwise.
setup.deck: A unique set of thirty-two tiles where eleven specific tiles are duplicated to form matched pairs.
setup.equipment: 32 Chinese dominoes, a 'Chung' marker for the banker, and three dice to determine the deal order.
setup.dealing: Tiles are stacked in a 4x8 woodpile; dice are rolled to select which player receives the first stack.

rules.objective: Arrange four tiles into two pairs that both beat the banker's corresponding pairs according to traditional tile rankings.
rules.gameplay: 1. Woodpile: Tiles are shuffled and stacked in a woodpile. 2. Deal: Players receive four tiles based on a dice roll. 3. Partition: Divide tiles into a high hand and a low hand. 4. Ranking: High hand must rank equal to or higher than the low hand. 5. Showdown: Banker compares pairs with each player. 6. Settlement: Win both pairs to win; lose both to lose; split results in a push.
keyRules: The high hand must always be equal to or higher in rank than the low hand partition.
To win the wager, both player pairs must outrank the banker's pairs; one win and one loss is a push.
Ties on a specific pair comparison (copy hands) are won by the banker.
The Luk and Saam tiles known together as Gee Joon are semi-wild and can be used as three or six to optimize hand totals.
The precedence of combinations is as follows: Gee Joon followed by Traditional Bo Pairs then Wongs then Gongs and finally High Nines.

strategy.basic: Learn to recognize the matched pairs immediately and understand the mod-10 scoring for non-ranking hands.
strategy.intermediate: Balance the strength between your high and low hands; a very strong high hand often leaves a vulnerable low hand.
strategy.advanced: Master the 'House Way' for dealer play and use it as a baseline for your own strategic partitions.
tips: Never split matched pairs unless they can form even stronger individual ranking combinations.
Use the Gee Joon wild tiles to bridge gaps in your modular totals to reach nine.
Track which high-ranking tiles have been played to estimate the banker's remaining strength.

ante.reason: Pai Gow uses standard gambling wagers placed before the deal rather than an ante system.

deal.reason: The woodpile dealing process is handled automatically by the engine or the house dealer.

reveal_market.reason: Traditional Chinese Pai Gow does not utilize a market or common pool of available tiles.

buy_market.reason: There is no mechanic for purchasing tiles from a market in the game of Pai Gow.

buy_stock.reason: Players do not purchase tiles; all tiles are distributed during the initial dealing phase.

fold.reason: Folding is not allowed; players must participate in the showdown once tiles are partitioned.

check.reason: Wagering occurs prior to the tile distribution, so checking is not an available option.

call.reason: There are no mid-hand betting rounds where a player would need to call a wager.

bet.description: Place a wager on the outcome of the tile comparisons against the banker.
bet.constraints: Must be placed before the woodpile dealing begins and within table limits.
bet.reason: This is the initial action that defines the player's stake in the current game round.

raise.reason: Wagers are fixed at the start of the round and cannot be raised during play.

declare.reason: Success is determined by physical tile comparison rather than any form of verbal declaration.

reveal_hand.reason: Hand reveal is an engine-driven phase that occurs after all partitions are set by players.

award_pot.reason: Winning wagers are paid directly by the banker rather than through a collective pot.

play_card.reason: Tiles are partitioned and compared as pairs rather than being played one at a time.

draw.reason: The game does not include a draw mechanic; players use only the four tiles dealt.

discard.reason: All four tiles must be used in the hand partition; no tiles are discarded.

pass.reason: Players must actively partition their tiles and cannot pass their turn to act.

bid.reason: Pai Gow does not involve bidding for contracts or to determine a declarer role.

meld.reason: The game uses poker-style partition pairs rather than rummy-style sets or runs.

go_out.reason: The game deal concludes automatically once all bets are settled against the banker.

wildcards.restrictions: Can act as 3 or 6 to optimize the total; part of Gee Joon pair.

customActions.description: Deal four tiles from the woodpile to each player according to the dice-determined starting position.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; performed once per round after bank selection.
customActions.reason: This is the dealer action that distributes tiles from the woodpile.

customActions.description: Assign the role of banker to a player or the house for the current round.
customActions.constraints: Rotates counter-clockwise among players; players may choose to pass the bank.
customActions.reason: This establishes the banker who will have the advantage of winning copy hands.

customActions.description: Partition the four dealt tiles into a high-ranking pair and a low-ranking pair.
customActions.constraints: The ranking of the high hand must be equal to or greater than the low hand.
customActions.reason: This is the primary strategic decision-making action where players optimize their tile layout.

customActions.description: Expose the partitioned tile pairs for comparison against the banker's corresponding pairs.
customActions.constraints: Occurs after all active players have finalized their tile partitions for the round.
customActions.reason: This moves the game deal into the final resolution and settlement phase.

customActions.description: Finalize wagers based on pair comparisons and collect or distribute casino chips.
customActions.constraints: Automatic resolution action performed by the engine after hands are fully compared.
customActions.reason: This action concludes the betting round by reconciling all player stakes with the banker.

engine.handRankingSystem: Traditional Chinese hierarchy including Gee Joon, matched pairs, unmatched pairs, Wongs, Gongs, and mod-ten points.
engine.rankingSystem: Complex partition-based comparison involving thirty-two unique tile combinations and traditional symbolic names.
engine.deckDescription: The set consists of thirty-two specialized Chinese domino tiles with unique symbolic names and specifically duplicated pairs used for traditional banking play.
engine.suitDescription: The tiles do not use suits but are divided into military and civil sets for ranking purposes.
engine.rankDescription: Tile ranks follow a traditional hierarchy where symbolic importance outranks numeric pip totals in most cases.
engine.dealPattern: Tiles are dealt in stacks of four from a 4x8 woodpile based on dice roll results.

notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Pai Gow is a partition banking game and does not utilize fishing or capture mechanics.
notApplicableReasons.patienceConfig: This is a competitive gambling game and is not designed for single-player solitaire play.

hero.title: Pai Gow
hero.subtitle: Ancient Tile Banking

synthesis.shortDescription: Traditional Chinese domino game. Partition four tiles into two pairs to beat the banker's hands.

prompts.human: How do I rank tiles in Pai Gow?
prompts.ai: Pai Gow uses a complex hierarchy. Matched pairs are highest, followed by symbolic unmatched pairs (like Heaven and Earth), then Wongs, Gongs, and finally the last digit of the tile totals (mod 10). The Gee Joon tiles are the supreme pair!

scoring.description: Win both pair comparisons to win the bet; split outcomes result in a push where the bet is returned.
scoring.winCondition: Both the player's high and low hands must outrank the banker's corresponding hands to win.

penalties.fouled_hand: Forfeit of the entire wager if the low hand outranks the high hand partition.

scoring.splitRules: Exact ties on individual pair comparisons are won by the banker (copy hands).

nullReasons.targetScore: Winning is determined by individual hand comparisons rather than a cumulative point score.
nullReasons.cardValues: Pai Gow uses tile pair rankings and mod-10 point comparison, not per-tile point values.
